page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text with a full-width list of herbs and remedies. A running head sits at the top, the page number at the top right, and a catchword at the foot below the rule. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: Graminis, Helenii, Lilii, Petrofelini, Poeoniae, Raphani, Valerianae, &c.
15. Venenis resistentes: Angelicae, Apii, Allii, Aristolochiae longae, Bryoniae, Cyperi, Costi, Foeniculi, Gentianae, Carlinae, Doronici, &c.
16. Ambusta sanantes; Asphodeli, Bulbi, Hyacinthi, Liliorum alborum.
17. Dolorem mitigantes; ut, Acori, Dauci, Eryngii, Ireos, Mandragorae, Ononis.
Occulta qualitate alterat: radix Bryoniae, Paeoniae, &c.
Corrumpendo vero alterant Venena,ut: Mandragorae, Fungi, Ephemerum, Veratrum album.
Purgantes radices sequuntur quae vel Bilem vel Pituitam expurgant.

page.notes: The catchword "uestris," is the continuation of the word "fyl-" at the line end. The number "15." is set in a form that is hard to read ([?] not applied to the number itself, as it is a printed numeral). Long s was read as plain s throughout, so forms such as "fistentes", "fanantes" and "Ariftolochiae" were corrected to sistentes, sanantes and Aristolochiae. "Costi" is read from the printed "Cofti". Rendering of "Ambusta sanantes" and "Atram" is a close reading and was not checked against a second copy.
